_how_to_use: PASTE ONLY THE `prompt` FIELD INTO THE IMAGE MODEL. Nothing else in this file is for the model. Pasting the whole file produced a collage of several captioned slides, because `renditions_wanted` lists two sizes, `framing.aspect_ratios` lists two ratios, and headline_in_app / caption_in_app are text - the model read all of that as a brief to draw multiple frames with words on them. Those fields are for the render pipeline and for whoever writes the app copy.
_source_image_note: Save the image you keep in this folder named `03_welcome_3_library_stays_yours` with whatever extension the model gave you - .jpg, .png, .jpeg and .webp are all accepted. Only the NAME has to match this file; the extension does not. lessons/scripts/tutor_images.py then renders it to renders/03_welcome_3_library_stays_yours/ as slide_1080x1920 (9:16 phone slide) and card_1080x1350 (4:5). Renditions are always written as PNG regardless of the source format.
audience: the learner setting up their own account
caption_in_app: Every lesson you attend is saved to rewatch any time - even between subscriptions.
intent: going back over an earlier lesson by choice - revision on your own terms, upright and purposeful
prompt: A single photograph, one continuous scene, filling the whole frame. A South African teenager sitting upright at a table on a bright weekend afternoon, going back over an earlier lesson: exercise book open at pages already written on, pen in hand, a phone or tablet propped up beside the book with the screen turned away from camera so nothing on it is readable. Daylight through a window, curtains open. Calm and deliberate - the posture of someone choosing to revise, not catching up in a panic and not lounging.
negative_prompt: any text, letters, numbers, words, signage, logos, watermarks, user-interface elements, phone screens showing apps, charts or graphs, cartoon, illustration, 3d render, cgi, airbrushed skin, plastic sheen, cinematic colour grade, film still look, motion blur, lens flare, extra fingers, malformed hands, distorted faces, stock-photo smiles, American classrooms, generic 'African' styling, collage, multiple panels, split screen, side-by-side frames, contact sheet, grid of images, storyboard, several phone mockups, device frames, app screenshots, before-and-after, picture-in-picture, borders, margins, framed print, lying down, lying on a bed, slouching, sprawled, in pyjamas, under a duvet, phone in bed, night-time bedroom, idle scrolling

_pipeline_only._note: NOT model input - read by the render script and the app.

framing.composition: subject in the lower two thirds, calm uncluttered space in the upper third where the slide's headline and caption sit - the image must never compete with the copy
framing.safe_area: keep the top 28% and bottom 18% visually quiet: the headline sits above, the button below

_revision_note: Rewritten 2026-07-30 (owner): the first version had the learner lying on a bed late at night with an earphone in. On a study product that reads as lounging and teaches the wrong habit on the third slide a student ever sees. Same promise - the lesson is yours to return to - shown as upright daytime revision instead. Follow-up: 'No bed, nobody lying down, nothing about night-time' was removed from the POSITIVE prompt. Image models handle negation badly, and naming a bed is a reliable way to get one; exclusions belong in negative_prompt, where these already are.
